I'm not going to flip my view just because everyone around you disagrees — that would be a pretty bad reason to change a belief. If the evidence pointed the other way, I'd reconsider, but the pattern I see is still pretty clear: more comparison-driven anxiety, faster polarization, and platforms designed to fragment attention for profit.

I get why people feel positive about it — it connects people and spreads information quickly — but that doesn't erase the costs. Consensus doesn't make something true, especially when the people most invested in the platforms have every reason to frame them positively.
